comparison: Perfect agreement on bioinformatic pipeline and survival analyses (C9, C12, C13, C14). Both evaluations find the TCGA/CPTAC data analysis and prognostic correlations convincing and well-supported.
Complete agreement on cell cycle synchronization experiments (C22, C23, C24, C57). Both accept the timing and phosphorylation pattern data in AMBRA1 KO cells as clarifying GTSE1 regulation.
Full agreement on CPTAC data analysis for phosphorylation site enrichment (C25, C26). Both find the clinical validation of experimental findings credible and appropriately analyzed.

Complete concordance on mechanism of GTSE1 stabilization via cyclin D1-CDK4 (C29, C30, C31, C32). Both evaluations accept the convergent evidence from multiple experimental systems including mAID and Palbociclib rescue.
Perfect agreement on GTSE1 protein stabilization data (C33, C34, C35, C36). Both accept the CHX chase experiments and mutant comparisons as demonstrating phosphorylation-dependent stability.
Full agreement on mechanistic distinction (C37, C38). Both accept that GTSE1 stabilization is indirect through CDK4/6 activity rather than direct AMBRA1 substrate recognition.
Complete agreement on CPTAC correlation with proliferation markers (C39, C60). Both find the statistical analysis across cancer types convincing and consistent with functional data.

Both evaluations rate this as UNCERTAIN (C40). OpenEval notes the contradiction with published literature on GTSE1 migration; peer reviewers do not comment, and authors acknowledge lack of statistical significance.
Perfect agreement on proliferation phenotype (C41, C42, C43, C44). Both accept the convergent evidence from multiple orthogonal assays demonstrating functional impact on cell growth.

Strong agreement on phosphorylation evidence (C15, C16, C17, C18, C58). OpenEval emphasizes orthogonal approaches and controls; peer reviewers explicitly call evidence 'convincing.' Peer R2 also includes site mapping claims (C19, C20, C21, C27, C28) that OpenEval addresses separately.

Partial overlap on C56. OpenEval R12 emphasizes CDK-specific site distinction; peer R13 accepts this as part of phosphorylation characterization without detailed commentary.
Strong agreement on background/literature claims (C1, C2, C3, C45, C46, C53, C54). Both treat these as established context rather than novel findings requiring evaluation.
Strong agreement on prior literature context (C4, C5, C6, C7, C8, C10, C11, C55). Both accept these as appropriately cited background establishing GTSE1 relevance.

Partial agreement on interpretive model. OpenEval R15 synthesizes broad mechanistic claims (C47-C52, C59); peer R11 specifically affirms GTSE1 as 'non-pocket substrate' in pathological contexts (C47, C52).
Strong agreement on central mechanism (C48, C49, C50, C51). Both accept the overall model of cyclin D1-CDK4 regulation of GTSE1 as convincing and well-supported by totality of data.
Agreement on mechanistic interpretation (C59). Both accept that phosphorylation-dependent stabilization follows logically from experimental findings without challenge.
